notes: Mass-mailed retirement income workshop invitation with an undisclosed retroactive plan result and a one-sided bond ladder description, against an accurately qualified annuity guarantee and a balanced Social Security delay point.

planted.span: A couple who retired on January 1, 2000 with $1,000,000 and followed the Three-Bucket Income Plan we use today could have withdrawn $35,000 a year, raised it each year for inflation, and still had $1.4 million at the end of 2025.
planted.explanation: Applying the firm's current plan retroactively to a 2000 retiree is hypothetical performance, sent to a general prospect audience with no criteria or assumptions (allocation, returns used, fees, taxes) and no statement of its risks and limitations.

planted.span: A ladder of individual bonds, each held until it matures, gives you a predictable schedule of income, lets you match maturities to the years you will need the money and takes the guesswork out of retirement spending.
planted.explanation: The ladder's benefits are stated without its material risks (issuer default or downgrade, early calls, inflation eroding fixed payments, reinvestment at lower rates, losses if bonds are sold before maturity), which the invitation covers only with a generic footer.

decoys.span: An income annuity can turn part of your savings into payments guaranteed for as long as you live.
decoys.why_ok: The guarantee is accurately qualified in the next sentences as depending on the insurer's claims-paying ability and not backed by the firm, the FDIC or any government agency, with illiquidity and inflation limits stated.

decoys.span: Your benefit grows for each year you wait past full retirement age, up to age 70.
decoys.why_ok: The benefit of delaying is immediately balanced by the cost of collecting for fewer years and the personal factors that decide whether delay pays off.
